fixes.explanation: Close, but the Jordan doesn't come up here. What God says is that He brought them “…out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.” The people are at the mountain while He speaks (Exodus 19:2). So the rescue He points to is the one behind them.

I get why that sounds right, but that's not what God says first. His opening command is, “You shall have no other gods before Me.” Nothing about a morning offering shows up in these verses. The first thing He asks is that Israel have no other gods before Him, none at all.

A king is a big thing to want, friend, but it's not what this command is about. God says, “You shall not make for yourself an idol in the form of anything in the heavens above, on the earth below, or in the waters beneath.” The thing being made here is an idol. That's the word to hold onto.

You've got it. God says, “for I, the LORD your God, am a jealous God…” He says it right after telling them not to bow down to idols or worship them. So the word comes from Him, in His own description of Himself. Good work, baker.

That one sounds sweet, friend, like a family love loop. But the verse gives a different reason. God says, “Honor your father and mother, so that your days may be long in the land that the LORD your God is giving you.” The reason attached is long days in that land. It's about the one honoring, and about a land the LORD is giving.

The text never says enemy here. God says, “You shall not covet your neighbor’s house.” and ends with “…anything that belongs to your neighbor.” The word He uses is neighbor, and that's the one to hold onto.

Not quite, friend. The text says, “…they trembled and stood at a distance.” Thunder, lightning and smoke, and the people tremble and stand at a distance. They don't rush closer. So the answer is False.
